title: Computing with many encoded logical qubits beyond break-even
abstract: Demonstrates quantum computations that outperform their unencoded counterparts using high-rate quantum error correcting codes on a trapped-ion system. Employs high-rate iceberg quantum error detecting codes and two-level concatenated iceberg QEC codes on the 98-qubit Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion quantum processor, yielding 94 error-detected logical qubits and 48 error-corrected logical qubits from 98 physical qubits. Verifies functionality through a partially-fault-tolerant quantum simulation of the three-dimensional XY model of quantum magnetism using 64 error-detected logical qubits. GHZ state of 94 logical qubits achieved with fidelity 94.9%.
key_claims: 94 error-detected logical qubits and 48 error-corrected logical qubits from 98 physical qubits
Near-1:1 physical-to-logical ratio for error detection; 2:1 for error correction
Logical error rates 10-100x below physical counterparts — beyond break-even
3D XY model quantum simulation executed with 64 logical qubits
State-of-the-art logical component and state fidelities demonstrated
supports_or_contradicts: SUPPORTS — demonstrates that Helios (the hardware we flagged in HYP-013/016 for our circuit) is now achieving dramatically better logical qubit ratios than we modeled. Raises the ceiling for viable MERA simulations on Helios-class hardware.
